ceviri.33: Can an account be managed without a social media strategy?
ceviri.34: It can; but production without a goal cannot be measured, and there is no way to track what the effort returned.
ceviri.35: How many platforms should an SME be on?
ceviri.36: Two, at most three, is sustainable at SME scale. Adding a new platform without raising production capacity breaks the rhythm of the accounts you already have.
ceviri.37: How long does a social media strategy take to show results?
ceviri.38: On organic work, the first meaningful data usually appears after 90 days of steady production. Lasting growth becomes clear over the 6–12 months in which the rhythm is kept up; the timescale varies with the sector and how often you publish.
ceviri.39: Which headings should the strategy document contain?
ceviri.40: Seven headings are enough: a one-sentence aim, the buyer audience profile, the platforms chosen and the reasoning behind the choice, three to five topics as content pillars, the weekly production rhythm, the monthly measurement routine and the division of responsibility. The document shouldn't run past a single page; the longer it gets the less it is read, and what isn't read isn't applied. Going over those headings at the end of each quarter and comparing them against current data keeps the strategy off the shelf and gives the team a shared reference.
ceviri.41: How often should platform choice be reviewed?
ceviri.42: A light check every three months and a full assessment once a year is a balanced rhythm. When audience behaviour or the business goal changes, review it without waiting.
ceviri.43: Does platform choice work differently for B2B brands?
ceviri.44: It does; a B2B buyer takes longer over the decision and researches it. Professional networks and expert content come forward on the B2B route, while short-video channels stay in a supporting role.
ceviri.45: Should I build the strategy with an agency or with my own team?
ceviri.46: The in-house team knows the brand and the agency knows the method; the ideal arrangement is a partnership of the two. If your resources are limited, taking expert support during setup and gradually taking the running over yourself is a balanced start.

ceviri.60: What Is a Social Media Strategy, and What Settles Platform Choice?
ceviri.61: A social media strategy is the written road map that sets out who a brand will talk to, on which platform, with what content and towards what goal. As the number of businesses going digital in Türkiye climbs, opening an account and posting at random produces nothing. In this guide we set out the criteria for choosing organic platforms and the route a strategy follows, for the decision-makers of SMEs. Comparing advertising channels and reporting metrics are subjects for separate articles; the focus here is on drawing the right route. In this article you'll find the questions to answer, in order, as you build your strategy.
ceviri.62: Strategy is the route that determines which platform a brand advances on.
ceviri.64: What Is a Social Media Strategy?
ceviri.65: A social media strategy is the written decision framework that brings the target audience, the platform choice, the content pillars and the measures of success together in a single plan. A well-built social media strategy makes clear which channel you will be on and what you want to achieve there. With a written plan, the team works towards the same goal and production doesn't drift into day-to-day decisions.
ceviri.66: What strategy amounts to on social media stays abstract at most businesses; in practice it is the answer to five questions. The questions are these: who will we reach, where will we be, what will we say, how often will we produce, and what will we measure success with? When those answers aren't put in writing, the account surrenders to the daily flow. Producing content without building a strategy is like setting off without a map: there is movement, but no direction.
ceviri.67: A brand whose target audience is vague cannot have a clear strategy either. Once you define your buyer audience by age, interest and buying behaviour, the platform and content decisions get simpler. As clarity rises, production speeds up and argument falls away. That simplicity shortens the approval process inside the team too.
ceviri.68: Are Strategy and Content Calendar the Same Thing?
ceviri.69: A content calendar is the strategy's instrument of delivery; it isn't the strategy itself. The calendar says what will be posted on which day; the strategy defines which goal that post serves. Accounts with a publishing plan but no goal cannot measure progress despite producing steadily.
ceviri.70: Why Should You Start with a Single Aim?
ceviri.71: The aim means choosing one priority: awareness, generating demand, or building a community. A single priority simplifies both the content pillars and the platform decision. SMEs chasing three goals at once usually reach none of them; where resources are limited, ranking them is essential. Reconsidering the priority at the start of each quarter is enough.
ceviri.73: Platform choice is settled by where your audience spends its time, by your content format and by your team's production capacity. Three criteria are weighed together: audience density, format fit and the sustainability of production. One criterion alone is not enough. In a social media strategy the question shouldn't be "which platform is popular" but "where is my audience, and can I produce there".
ceviri.74: Audience density is the first criterion. A B2B decision-maker moves around professional networks; a young consumer spends time on short-video channels. A local customer, meanwhile, uses maps and visual discovery channels.
ceviri.76: — TurkStat is Türkiye's statistical institute — shows that internet and social network use is spreading across Türkiye; your audience is already online, and the question is which door you come in by. The pressure to digitalise is growing too.
ceviri.77: The Ministry of Trade's 2025 outlook report
ceviri.78: puts the number of businesses trading online at 634,611. As competitors move into the digital shop window, staying invisible creates a cost of its own.
ceviri.79: The second criterion is format fit, the third is capacity. We treat the paid channel side as a separate discipline, like
ceviri.81: ; the route in this article is the organic leg of the strategy.
ceviri.82: How Do You Do Audience Analysis?
ceviri.83: Audience analysis is the work of defining your buyer audience by age, location, interest and buying habits. Start with the customer data you already have: who buys, and what do they research before deciding? That profile is the compass for the platform decision.
ceviri.84: Where Do You Find the Audience Data?
ceviri.85: Account statistics, site analytics, customer conversations and sector reports are the four basic sources. Cross-referencing those four instead of guessing moves the choice from assumption to measurement.
ceviri.86: Why Are Format and Capacity Fit Decisive?
ceviri.87: A team that cannot produce video cannot sustain a presence on a video channel. Set the number of pieces you can produce in a week honestly; managing two platforms well is worth more than leaving five empty.
ceviri.88: How Do You Build the Strategy Route?
ceviri.89: The strategy route is built by settling, in order, the aim, the audience, the platforms, the content pillars and the measurement routine. The order matters: in a social media strategy, taking the platform decision before the aim turns the route around. Brands that set their social media strategy onto that five-step skeleton don't leave production to daily inspiration; every piece of content is tied to a goal.
ceviri.90: A social media strategy should be simple enough to fit onto a single page. Complete the five steps in this order:
ceviri.91: Choose the aim: awareness, demand or community; settle on a single priority.
ceviri.92: Define your buyer audience: age, location, interest and buying behaviour.
ceviri.93: Eliminate platforms: pick at most two or three channels using audience density, format fit and capacity.
ceviri.94: Write the content pillars: fix the three to five topics your brand returns to.
ceviri.95: Set up the measurement routine: decide up front which indicators you'll look at monthly.
ceviri.96: We turn that skeleton into a written document within the first month of our
ceviri.99: What Does the 90-Day Road Map Cover?
ceviri.100: The first 30 days are for setup and confirming the audience. The second 30 days go to content experiments, the last 30 to concentrating on the format that works. At the end of the ninety days your strategy rests not on guesswork but on measured data from your own account. That data shapes the plan for the second quarter.
ceviri.101: Which Mistakes Take SMEs Off Route?
ceviri.102: The most common mistake is trying to be on every platform at once and producing steadily on none of them. Distributing copied content and posting without a purpose are the most frequent symptoms of a weak social media strategy. At a business with limited resources, a social media strategy also writes down what you won't do; the platform given up is depth gained.
ceviri.103: An SME spread across five channels thins out on every account; a competitor focused on two goes deeper. The second trap is copying the same image onto every channel: the language of the channel differs and its audience behaves differently. The third trap is impatience; organic growth asks for steady production and for time.
ceviri.104: Set realistic thresholds on the resource side. The hours given to weekly production, the monthly content count and the review rhythm should all be written down at the start. For brands that want to connect organic work to sales, our
ceviri.106: service comes into play; it brings channel data together in a single conversion funnel. What keeps a strategy standing on social media isn't talent but rhythm. When the rhythm breaks, it isn't the algorithm that should be reviewed first — it's the plan.
ceviri.108: Three to five pieces a week, one review a month and a 90-day trial are sustainable thresholds at SME scale. If the threshold doesn't hold, reduce the number of platforms; narrowing the scope is the right choice, rather than breaking the rhythm.

ceviri.111: Build Your Social Media Strategy with an Expert Team
ceviri.112: Working with an expert team takes the setup of a strategy out of trial and error and rests it on measurement. The route is in writing from the first month. As an agency, we complete the audience analysis, platform elimination and content pillar steps together with you. Our team takes on the production rhythm. Your social media strategy then runs on a system rather than on one person.
ceviri.113: At TasarımMania we work on the principle of "measure first, produce second". In the first meeting we settle your aim and your buyer audience together. We do the platform elimination using audience density, format fit and capacity. After setup, the content calendar, the production and the community management are gathered in a single team; you review the route through a monthly strategy meeting.

ceviri.118: The process runs in three stages. First the discovery meeting and the audience analysis; then the strategy document and the calendar are set up; the last stage is the monthly rhythm of production and reporting. We deliver the first strategic output within three weeks.
